summary: Defines how IP and ARP packets are encapsulated for transmission over ARCNET local area networks, using the ARCNET packet header definition standard. It is an Internet standard.

eli5.summary: Computers on one kind of office network need a way to wrap Internet messages for it. This describes the wrapping.

questions: how is ip sent over arcnet
what is the arp hardware type for arcnet
subtitle: How IP and ARP datagrams are wrapped, split into fragments and addressed on ARCNET local networks.

tldr.problem: ARCNET frames carry at most 504 octets of client data, and the earlier method in RFC 1051 limited unfragmented IP packets to 508 octets.
tldr.mechanism: IP, ARP and RARP datagrams ride in the client data area of ARCNET packets, using the ARCNET Packet Header Definition Standard, which can split a packet into up to 120 fragments.
tldr.outcome: Packets of up to 60,480 octets are possible in principle, 8-bit ARCNET addresses are mapped with ARP, and the RFC replaces RFC 1051.

today: RFC 1201 is an Internet Standard that obsoletes RFC 1051, and the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This memo specifies a method of encapsulating Internet Protocol (RFC 791) and Address Resolution Protocol (RFC 826) datagrams for transmission across ARCNET, using the ARCNET Packet Header Definition Standard. It offers a replacement for RFC 1051, whose ARCNET framing protocol limits unfragmented IP packets to 508 octets.

The standard was agreed in 1989 by Apple Computers, Novell, ACTINET Systems, Standard Microsystems and Pure Data Research.
sections.eli5: ARCNET is an older kind of office network. This document says how to put Internet messages into its envelopes, in a better way than the first attempt.

sections.title: ARCNET Frames
sections.content:
ARCNET hardware supports two frame types: short frames, always 256 octets long, and long frames, always 512 octets long. Every frame starts with a hardware header and ends with the client's data preceded by a software header. Software puts padding in the middle to reach the fixed length, and the hardware removes it during transmission.

Short frames hold 0 to 249 octets of client data and long frames hold 253 to 504 octets. A third type, the exception frame, handles data of 250, 251 or 252 octets. The software header holds a protocol ID, a split flag and a two-octet sequence number.
sections.eli5: There are small envelopes and big envelopes. For sizes that fit neither well, there is a special third envelope.

sections.title: Fragmentation, Reassembly and Retransmission
sections.content:
ARCNET hardware limits a frame to 512 octets, or 504 octets of client data. The datalink protocol can break a packet into as many as 120 fragments, allowing up to 60,480 octets per packet. The split flag marks them. Unfragmented packets have a split flag of zero. The first fragment has ((T-2)*2)+1, where T is the total number of fragments. Later fragments have ((N-1)*2), where N is the fragment number, so the fourth fragment has six. The highest legal split flag value is EE hex, and FF hex marks exception packets. All fragments of one packet share a sequence number.

For reassembly, the RFC recommends allocating space for the whole packet when the first fragment arrives. Fragments are sent in order, so reassembly can give up if one arrives out of order, but it should ignore repeated fragments. It can also give up if no more fragments arrive within a few seconds.

The hardware tells the sender whether a unicast packet was acknowledged, so implementations are encouraged to retransmit unacknowledged packets or fragments. Broadcast packets are never acknowledged and should never be retransmitted. Retransmission can cause duplicates, which are not a problem for IP or ARP.
sections.eli5: A big letter is cut into numbered pieces and sent in order. The receiver ignores doubles and gives up if the pieces stop coming.

sections.title: Address Mapping, ARP and RARP
sections.content:
ARCNET addresses are 8 bits, so IP addresses must be mapped down. A unicast address is mapped using ARP. The RFC mentions that IP addresses could be assigned so the last eight bits equal the ARCNET address, but says this is not recommended because ARP is more flexible at very small cost. All IP broadcast addresses must map to the ARCNET broadcast address 0. ARCNET has no multicast support, so all IP multicast addresses must also map to address 0. Broadcasts may be lost, which does not greatly affect IP or ARP.

For ARP over ARCNET the hardware address length is 1 octet, the ARP hardware type is 7, and requests are broadcast to address 0.

RARP packets (RFC 903) can also be carried and are handled like ARP. The RFC notes three differences from Ethernet. There are only 255 hardware addresses on an ARCNET. They are more likely to be duplicated across ARCNET networks. And they are set by switches rather than fixed in ROM.
sections.eli5: Each computer has a small number as its address. A computer shouts a question to everyone, address 0, to find who owns a number. Shouting to everyone is also how group messages work.

sections.title: Maximum Transmission Unit
sections.content:
The maximum IP packet length with this method is 60,480 octets, which is impractical, so implementations on a network must agree on a smaller value and the maximum MUST be configurable. Implementations must be able to send and receive IP datagrams up to 576 octets and are strongly encouraged to handle 1500 octets. They may accept larger arriving datagrams.

To avoid datalink fragmentation, an implementation may aim at an IP packet size of 504 octets, at the cost of more packets for each node on the path. It might signal this with a TCP maximum segment size of 464 octets or announce an MTU of 504 octets through a mechanism such as RFC 1063.
sections.eli5: Everyone on the network agrees how big a parcel can be. Smaller parcels avoid cutting, but then there are more of them.

sections.title: Assigned Numbers and Security
sections.content:
Datapoint Corporation assigns ARCNET protocol IDs. For this specification it assigned 212 decimal to IP, 213 to ARP and 214 to RARP. These differ from the numbers used by RFC 1051, so both can exist on one ARCNET but cannot talk to each other. IANA assigned ARCNET the ARP hardware type 7.

The memo says that security issues are not discussed.
sections.eli5: Each kind of message gets its own label number so the receiver knows what is inside. The old and new methods use different labels, so they ignore each other.
